description: Aviation covers how aircraft fly, building and flying a model or drone, flight operations such as preflight inspections and simulators, visiting airports and aviation facilities, and the paths to flying and aviation careers.

safety.note: Drone flights must follow FAA rules; earn the required recreational drone certification before flying.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Aviation basics
requirements.summary: Kinds of aircraft, the history of flight, engines, the four forces, lift, control surfaces and cockpit instruments.

requirements.title: Principles of flight
requirements.summary: One option: a model glider, a rubber-band airplane, or a powered model or drone with the required certification.

requirements.title: Flight operations
requirements.summary: Two options such as flight-simulator practice, a preflight inspection, observing maintenance, reading charts or a discovery flight.

requirements.title: Airport operations
requirements.summary: One option: visiting an airport, an FAA facility, a military aviation facility, or an aviation museum or air show.

requirements.title: Aviation opportunities
requirements.summary: Pilot certificates and ratings, aviation youth programs and aviation careers.
